etymologies.etymologyHTML: From Middle English original, from Old French original, from Late Latin orīginālis (“primitive, original”), from Latin orīgō (“beginning, source, origin”); see origin.

definitions.definition: (not comparable) Relating to the origin or beginning; preceding all others.

quote.citation: 1944, Miles Burton, chapter 5, in The Three Corpse Trick‎[2], →ISBN, →OCLC, →OL:
quote.text: The hovel stood in the centre of what had once been a vegetable garden, but was now a patch of rank weeds. Surrounding this, almost like a zareba, was an irregular ring of gorse and brambles, an unclaimed vestige of the original common.

definitions.definition: (not comparable) First in a series of copies or versions.

quote.citation: 1963, Margery Allingham, chapter 1, in The China Governess: A Mystery, London: Chatto & Windus, →OCLC:
quote.text: The original family who had begun to build a palace to rival Nonesuch had died out before they had put up little more than the gateway, […].

definitions.definition: (not comparable) Having a specified place or time as its origin.
(of a potato chip) Seasoned with salt but no other flavoring; ready salted
An object or other creation (e.g. narrative work) from which all later copies and variations are derived.
A person with a unique and interesting personality or creative talent.

quote.citation: 1700, Tom Brown, Amusements Serious and Comical, calculated for the Meridian of London, page 5:
quote.text: I have a great mind to be in Print; but above all, I would fain be an Original, and that is a true Comical Thought: When all the Learned Men in the World are but Tranſlators, is it not a Pleaſant Jeſt, that you ſhould ſtrive to be an Original! You ſhould have obſerved your Time, and have come into the World with the Ancient Greeks for that purpoſe; for the Latines themſelves are but Copies.
Ahmad (1969) studied the personality differences among middle school girls identified as originals and unoriginals on the Minnesota's test of creative thinking.

quote.citation: 2010, A. Kusuma, Creativity and Cognitive Styles in Children, page 73:
quote.text: The originals or the creatives were more dominant than the unoriginals or the low creatives.

quote.citation: 1899 February, Joseph Conrad, “The Heart of Darkness”, in Blackwood’s Edinburgh Magazine, volume CLXV, number M, New York, N.Y.: The Leonard Scott Publishing Company, […], →OCLC, part I, page 201:
quote.text: ‘Are you an alienist?’ I interrupted. ‘Every doctor should be - a little,’ answered that original, imperturbably.

definitions.definition: A newly designed garment released by a fashion designer as part of a collection.

quote.citation: 1962, “It's Fashion fair time again”, in Ebony, volume 17, number 11, page 126:
quote.text: Fashion Fair will give every section first hand knowledge of the latest originals and 1962-63's exciting trends.

quote.citation: 1963, National Retail Merchants Association. Sales Promotion Division, The NRMA Sales Promotion Encyclopedia, Vol. II., page 175:
quote.text: One such show was built around the Du Pont spring collection of Paris originals.
